title: Incident drill: token surge detection and investigation playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight incident drill playbook for token-surge events (sustained or sudden increases in token throughput) that degrade latency, increase cost, or trigger fallback flows. It combines SLI thresholds, targeted trace anchoring, adaptive sampling rules, and compact dashboard panels so operators can triage and remediate quickly.

Scope and when to run this drill:
- Triggered when 1-minute p50/p95 token-per-request or tokens/sec exceed baseline by >= 3x AND request latency SLOs (p95) breach for > 5 minutes.
- Also relevant for observed increases in fallback-model usage or repeated long tail stalls during KV cache miss storms.

High-level goals:
- Rapidly identify whether the surge is: traffic-driven (customer spike), workload-driven (prompt or model change), or infrastructure-driven (GPU contention, slow kernel).
- Reduce mean time to restore (MTTR) via prioritized probes and a minimal evidence set to decide fallback, autoscale, or rollback.
- Protect cost budgets by surfacing per-tenant cost burn and enabling quick rate-limits or tenant isolation.

Minimal evidence set (what we need in first 5 minutes):
1) Ingestion metrics: total tokens/sec, tokens/request distribution, active connections by route/model.
2) Latency breakouts: per-token processing time vs. fixed request overhead.
3) KV-cache signals: hit-rate, cold-cache request counts (first-request after cold start), cache-warm tails.
4) Resource signals: GPU utilization, GPU memory pressure, kernel queue length, host-level CPU/io.
5) Trace anchors: representative spans for slow requests, including prompt length and model id.
6) Per-tenant spend burn (1h projected burn) and token quanta by tenant.

Metric definitions (canonical names and notes):
- inference.tokens_total/sec: gauge (per-route, per-model) - rolling 1s and 60s.
- inference.tokens_per_request.pX: histogram (p50/p90/p95/p99) - bucketed by model and sequence-length bin.
- inference.token_processing_ms: timer per token (exclude fixed overhead).
- inference.request_overhead_ms: timer per request (auth, dispatch, network).
- kv.cache.hit_ratio: ratio on lookup count (label: tenant, model).
- kv.cold_requests_count: counter of requests marked cold (first K tokens missing).
- runtime.gpu.utilization_pct: gauge (per-GPU).
- runtime.gpu.queue_depth: gauge representing kernel queue length.
- cost.tenant.tokens_hourly: counter for tenant token usage (used for burn rate).
- fallback.invocations: counter for automatic fallbacks to smaller model or cached-response path.

Suggested alerting thresholds (starting points, tune to tenant/workload):
- token surge alert: inference.tokens_total/sec (cluster) > baseline * 3 for 2m -> P1 paging.
- latency breach alert: inference.request_latency.p95 (service) > target_latency * 1.5 for 5m -> P0.
- kv storm alert: kv.cold_requests_count rate > baseline * 5 for 3m -> P1.
- gpu-saturation alert: runtime.gpu.utilization_pct > 92% with queue_depth > threshold -> P1.
- cost burn warning: cost.tenant.tokens_hourly projected burn > 120% of daily budget -> P2 notify-runbook.

Trace and span conventions for token-surge investigations:
- Anchor spans at these points: request.receive, dispatch.route, model.invoke.start, model.tokenize, model.attention-kernel, model.invoke.end, kms.decrypt (if present).
- Attach these tags/fields to the root span: tenant_id, route, model_id, prompt_token_count, kv_cache_hit=true|false, used_quantization_profile.
- For slow-token traces, capture first 50 tokens worth of KV cache keys (hashed) and prompt length; do NOT capture raw prompt text. Redact PII.
- Sampling strategy: when token surge alert fires, temporarily bias sampling towards traces where kv_cache_hit=false OR latency > p95. Suggested: default sample_rate=0.1, surge_sample_rate=1.0 for flagged spans, but cap sampled payload size to 32KB.

Dashboard panels (compact operator dashboard):
- Top row: total tokens/sec (1s & 60s), tokens_per_request p50/p95, active routes heatmap.
- Middle row: token_processing_ms histogram, request_overhead_ms timeseries, GPU utilization per host.
- Bottom row: kv.cache.hit_ratio (per-tenant small-multiples), kv.cold_requests_count, fallback.invocations rate and percent.
- Sidebar widgets: per-tenant cost burn (projected), top-10 tenants by token QPS, currently open paging incidents.
- Drill links on each panel to a query that returns 50 representative trace ids (trace sampler id + time window).

Investigation checklist (step-by-step):
1) Confirm alert validity (false positives): check ingestion pipeline, metrics scraping delays, and metrics cardinality spikes.
2) Look at tokens/sec and tokens_per_request distribution to see if surge is many small requests or few long ones.
3) Check model change events and recent deploys (link release manifest). If a new model variant rolled, pause rollout.
4) Inspect KV cache hit_ratio and cold_requests_count. A cold-cache storm often looks like many long requests with kv_cache_hit=false.
5) Pull a small set of traces via dashboard drill links. Verify span timings: is time spent in attention-kernel or in pre/post processing?
6) Check host/GPU metrics for contention. If GPU queue_depth rising and utilization ~90% -> consider autoscale or throttling.
7) If tenant-localized spike: apply per-tenant rate-limit or isolate onto separate node-pool.
8) If global model latency regression: trigger rollback and replace traffic with smaller/better-performing variant.
9) After immediate mitigation, open a post-incident ticket linking: traces, graphs, tenant ids affected, and hypothesis.

Quick remediation knobs (ordered by immediacy and safety):
- Soft throttle at ingress for offending tenant or route (95th-quantile backpressure).
- Increase dedicated capacity (scale up GPU pool) if autoscale lag is root cause.
- Temporary fallback route to smaller model variant or cached-summary responses.
- Enable aggressive prefix/KV cache pre-warm for hot tenants (if safe).
- Rollback recent model or kernel change if trace evidence points to a new regression.

Playbook runbook snippet for oncall (copy-paste):
- PagerDuty: acknowledge -> Post to #ops-observability with incident tag -> Run "token-surge quick-check" script (links in dashboard) -> If tenant-localized, apply tenant throttle rule: autopolicy:tenant-throttle: <tenant-id> 60s=20000 tokens -> If global and GPU-saturation, scale pool and notify infra.

Post-mortem signals to collect:
- Representative traces (10 with worst p95 latency).
- Sequence-length distribution before/after surge.
- KV cache metrics with tenant labels.
- Cost burn delta and projected 24h overspend.
- Deploy timeline and any correlated platform changes.

Open questions and follow-ups (backlog candidates):
- Can we add an adaptive sampling controller that increases trace sampling only for spans where kv_cache_hit=false and latency > p95 to reduce noise?
- Build a compact per-tenant summary card (last 1h tokens, p95 latency, cost burn) to show in operator launcher.
- Instrument token-level internal timers so we can separate attention-kernel vs. kv-hydration time more precisely.
- Add a safeguard for autoscale costs: automated cool-down if projected 24h spend > threshold.

Notes and references:
- Quick queries for dashboard drill links (examples to convert to panel queries):
  * traces for slow tokens: service=runtime AND trace_duration_ms>2000 AND kv_cache_hit=false (limit 50)
  * cold-cache candidates: kv.cold_requests_count[1m] > 0 AND inference.tokens_per_request.p95>768
  * tenant burn: cost.tenant.tokens_hourly by tenant order desc

- Operational caution: avoid capturing raw prompts in traces or logs. Use hashed keys for prompts and cache keys, always apply text redaction rules.

Contact and ownership:
- Primary: Aisha Patel (eng-observability)
- Secondary: Marco Chen (serving-runtime), Elena Garcia (platform-engineering)

This doc is intended as a living drill script. Add concrete query strings and dashboard links as we iterate.
